subject.title: feat: add Fedora/RHEL-family platform support with rootless Podman

question: Should openclaw-ansible accept Fedora/RHEL-family rootless Podman/firewalld as a supported installer contract now, and under what proof and image-update policy?
rationale: The PR is a broad new supported runtime and security boundary; automation can identify concrete doc/onboarding defects but cannot approve the platform support contract or default mutable image policy.

options.title: Repair and prove before merge
options.body: Fix the remaining RedHat welcome/manual-doc/port mismatches, settle the default image-update policy, and require redacted Debian/Ubuntu plus Fedora/RHEL disposable-host proof before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Accept the new runtime contract explicitly
options.body: Maintainers may choose to own rootless Podman/firewalld support now, but should do so with clear operator-facing upgrade, reboot, firewall, and image-pull expectations.

options.title: Pause until platform scope is sponsored
options.body: If RedHat/Podman support is not yet a supported installer direction, pause this branch and restart from a smaller maintainer-backed design.

recommendation.title: Repair and prove before merge
recommendation.body: Fix the remaining RedHat welcome/manual-doc/port mismatches, settle the default image-update policy, and require redacted Debian/Ubuntu plus Fedora/RHEL disposable-host proof before reconsidering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Andy Lauppe has the strongest current history signal around the standalone install flow and bootstrap behavior that would own the support-contract decision.
